questions.question: What does a TreeSet use internally to store its elements?
options: A HashMap with a dummy value
A resizable array kept in order
A NavigableMap, normally a TreeMap, with a dummy value
questions.explanation: TreeSet stores each element as a key in a TreeMap. Every key maps to one shared dummy value named PRESENT.

questions.question: What does this print? TreeSet<Integer> s = new TreeSet<>(); s.add(40); s.add(10); s.add(40); s.add(25); System.out.println(s);
questions.explanation: The repeated 40 is rejected and the remaining elements are kept in ascending order.

questions.question: A TreeSet s holds 12, 18, 27 and 33. What does System.out.println(s.floor(20) + " " + s.higher(27)); print?
questions.explanation: floor(20) is the greatest element at or below 20, which is 18. higher(27) is the smallest element strictly above 27, which is 33.

questions.question: How does a TreeSet decide that a new element is a duplicate?
questions.explanation: TreeSet relies only on the ordering. An element that compares as 0 with an existing one is not added.

questions.question: What does this print? TreeSet<String> s = new TreeSet<>(Comparator.comparingInt(String::length)); s.add("Hall"); s.add("Desk"); s.add("Bench"); System.out.println(s.size());
questions.explanation: Desk has the same length as Hall, so the comparator returns 0 and Desk is dropped. Hall and Bench remain.

questions.question: Why does this throw at run time? TreeSet<String> s = new TreeSet<>(); s.add("Row"); s.add(null);
options: Natural ordering calls compareTo on null, which throws NullPointerException
A TreeSet needs a size before adding
Only one element can be added
questions.explanation: TreeSet compares every new element with existing ones. With natural ordering a null element cannot be compared.

questions.question: A Desk class does not implement Comparable, and new TreeSet<Desk>() is created with no Comparator. What happens on add(new Desk())?
questions.explanation: TreeSet casts elements to Comparable to order them. Without Comparable or a Comparator, the cast fails at run time.

questions.question: What is the time cost of add, remove and contains on a TreeSet with n elements?
questions.explanation: Each operation walks down a balanced red-black tree whose height stays near log n.

questions.question: Which statement about floor(x) and lower(x) is true?
options: Both ignore an element equal to x
floor(x) may return x itself, lower(x) never does
lower(x) may return x itself, floor(x) never does
Both throw an exception when nothing is found
questions.explanation: floor finds the greatest element at or below x. lower finds the greatest element strictly below x. Both return null if none exists.

questions.question: A TreeSet<Hall> sorts halls only by seat count. Halls Annex(60) and Lab(60) are added, but only Annex is stored. What is the best fix?
options: Switch to new TreeSet<>() with no Comparator
Add a tie-breaker, such as thenComparing by name, to the Comparator
questions.explanation: Equal seat counts compare as 0, so Lab looks like a duplicate. A tie-breaker makes different halls compare as non-zero.
